newsitem.title: USA: Freightliner to expand heavy truck output.
newsitem.headline: Freightliner to expand heavy truck output.

text.p: Freightliner Tuesday said its acquisition of Ford Motor Co's heavy truck business is proceeding and, as a result, its North Carolina plants will substantially increase heavy truck production and also be the new manufacturing site for the Ford Cargo truck.
Freightliner is a unit of Daimler-Benz.

In a statement, the company said Freightliner's Mt. Holly, N.C., truck manufacturing plant will gain the assembly operations for the low cab-over-engine Cargo truck, a Class 6-8 truck used for pickup and delivery, refuse hauling, and street sweeping, among others.
An estimated $3.1 million will be invested in equipment and assembly systems at the Mt. Holly plant for the Cargo trucks.

The company's Cleveland, N.C. truck manufacturing plant will increase its production of those Freightliner FLD-model Class 8 trucks currently built at the company's St. Thomas, Ontario manufacturing plant. The St. Thomas, Ontario plant will be the site dedicated to the production of the Ford HN80 truck series.

"We expect to increase employment at our Cleveland plant by about 600 people to accommodate the added Freightliner heavy truck production," Freightliner President Jim Hebe said, adding production levels at the Cleveland, N.C. plant will begin increasing in Fall 1997.

"Until we know the sales and production levels of the Cargo truck, it is too early to estimate the employment impact on our Mt. Holly plant." Ford had ceased production of the Cargo truck in February of this year.
